other.source: Typical Australian prices for a fast charger and an AC post on a network Charge Line doesn't list (Charge Line's charging price research, 27 October 2026)

networks.name: Tesla Supercharger
networks.source: Tesla prices each site by demand, shown in the Tesla app; a Supercharging Membership lowers the price for other EVs. tesla.com refuses automated readers.

networks.name: Evie
networks.source: Evie: about $0.40 at a 50 kW highway site to $0.75 ultra-fast in Melbourne; an Open Charge Map listing checked September 2026 says $0.62 at night and $0.71 by day. The site's prices are in the Evie app only. robots.txt asks for 10 seconds between requests.

networks.name: Chargefox
networks.source: Chargefox: site owners set the price; fast DC is 40–60c per kWh on average (Chargefox). Drivers report $0.60–0.74 at DC sites. Its terms forbid robots and scrapers.

networks.name: Ampol AmpCharge
networks.source: Ampol: prices vary by location, shown in the Ampol app; Open Charge Map listings say $0.60–0.75.

networks.name: BP Pulse
networks.source: bp pulse: pricing may vary between locations, some with peak and off-peak prices (bp pulse FAQs). bp's site refuses automated readers.

networks.name: NRMA
networks.source: NRMA: priced by location, $0.69–0.99 a kWh in the My NRMA app, members 5c less. Its public table of site prices may be read but not copied into an app without NRMA's permission.

networks.name: Jolt
networks.source: Jolt: 7 kWh free a day at fast chargers, then paid; Open Charge Map listings say $0.40–0.46 after the free 7 kWh. Its terms forbid scraping.
